newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore foreign shares down on Public Bank move.
newsitem.headline: Singapore foreign shares down on Public Bank move.

text.p: The foreign tranches of Singapore blue chip stocks slipped in early trade on Thursday after news Malaysia's Public Bank PUBM.SI was proposing to alter its rules to allow overseas investors to buy its local shares.
"One of the concerns is that if it can happen there, it can happen here," said one dealer with a major local bank.
The Public Bank proposal would let foreigners buy local shares, but denying them voting rights.
The stock of some politically or financially sensitive stocks, such as banks and national institutions, are split into local and foreign tranches in Singapore and elsewhere in Southeast Asia.
The idea is to limit the foreign ownership of these stocks.
Foreign tranches of stocks tend to hold a premium to local tranches because they can be bought by anyone.
But if the rules change, this premium should disappear, dealers said.
Most of the top losers on Thursday morning were foreign blue chip shares.

Singapore Press foreign led the pack, falling 50 cents to Singapore $29.00 by 0240 GMT, after reaching an early low of S$28.50. The foreign share tranches of all four big local banks lost between 20 and 40 cents each.
Public Bank foreign was last down three cents at S$2.29 on 6.1 million shares after dropping to a fresh 1997 low of S$2.18.
